t.6.109.1: When Rāma, the subduer of foes, had spent that night and risen refreshed, Vibhīṣaṇa, with joined palms, wished him victory and spoke these words to him.
t.6.109.2: Baths and unguents for the limbs, garments and ornaments, heavenly sandal pastes, and garlands of many kinds.
t.6.109.3: And these lotus-eyed women, skilled in the art of adornment, have come to attend you and will bathe you according to due rite, O Rāghava.
t.6.109.4: Thus addressed, Kākutstha replied to Vibhīṣaṇa: "You should invite the monkeys, headed by Sugrīva, to bathe."
t.6.109.5: But he, that righteous-souled one, accustomed to comfort, delicate and mighty-armed, a prince true to his promise, is suffering on my account.
t.6.109.6: Without him, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, who walks the path of dharma, neither bathing nor garments and ornaments are esteemed by me.
t.6.109.7: Let us quickly return by this very path to that city, Ayodhyā, for this road is long and extremely hard to travel.
t.6.109.8: Thus addressed, Vibhīṣaṇa replied to Kākutstha: "O son of a king, within a single day I shall bring you to that city."
t.6.109.9: Blessings upon you! There is an aerial chariot named Puṣpaka, radiant like the sun, belonging to my brother Kubera, which was carried off by force by Rāvaṇa.
t.6.109.10: Here stands this aerial chariot, resembling a cloud; by that vehicle you shall go to Ayodhyā, free from your distress.
t.6.109.11: If I am worthy of your favor, if you remember my good qualities, then stay here for a while, O wise one, if there is any affection in you for me.
t.6.109.12: Honored with every object of desire, you will then depart, O Rāma, together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa and your wife Vaidehī.
t.6.109.13: But, O Rāma, filled with affection for me, together with your army and your host of friends, accept for now this hospitality that I have arranged and offered to you.
t.6.109.14: Out of affection, deep esteem and friendship, O Rāghava, I, your servant, entreat you; I am surely not commanding you.
t.6.109.15: Addressed thus, Rāma then replied to Vibhīṣaṇa, while all the rākṣasas and the vānaras were listening.
t.6.109.16: O hero, scorcher of foes, I have been honored by you through your counsel, with your whole heart, with your offerings, and with the highest friendship.
t.6.109.17: It is surely not that I would refuse to do as you say, O lord of the rākṣasas; but my mind is in haste to see that brother of mine, Bharata.
t.6.109.18: He who came to Citrakūṭa to turn me back, he whose word I did not heed even as he entreated me with bowed head.
t.6.109.19: Kausalyā and Sumitrā and the illustrious Kaikeyī, my elders and my friends as well, and the citizens together with their sons.
t.6.109.20: Bring the vimāna to me quickly, O lord of the Rākṣasas. Now that my task is accomplished, staying here any longer can scarcely be agreeable to me.
t.6.109.21: Grant me leave, gentle one; I have been honored, Vibhīṣaṇa. You must surely not be offended; being in haste, I ask your consent.
t.6.109.22: Then the one whose parts were variegated with gold, which had platforms of vaiḍūrya gems, which was encircled by turreted chambers and gleamed like silver on every side.
t.6.109.23: It was richly adorned with pale-white pennants and banners, made splendid by golden mansions, and embellished with lotuses of gold.
t.6.109.24: It was strewn with clusters of tiny bells, its windows latticed with pearls and gems, encircled on every side by rows of larger bells, and sweetly ringing.
t.6.109.25: That aerial car, shaped like a peak of Meru and fashioned by Viśvakarman, was adorned with many mansions gleaming like pearls and silver.
t.6.109.26: It was furnished with floors whose surfaces were brightly inlaid with crystal, and with excellent seats of cat's-eye gems, richly precious and spread with costly coverings.
t.6.109.27: Having announced to Rāma that the invincible aerial chariot, swift as thought, had arrived, Vibhīṣaṇa stood there.
